# Web extension boundary: the compiler partitions core and web
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #142, sha256:d6ac7e25a40167c9ededa97e57d5a46ee3e82939e7b18404eb90344ab592d219). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->




- **Status:** Ready

- **Shape:** Story

- **Type:** feature (thin slice; no behaviour change)

- **Milestone:** Layered language: a domain-neutral core and one extension per domain

- **Source:** Steve's direction rulings relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-28 (web keywords belong in a web extension, not the core; look for clean breaks for other domains: desktop UI, mobile, data, testing, messaging, file IO, auth, background jobs) and Decider D89 (Codex No with conditions, Grok Support-it; the conditions are adopted). Agile: build only the web extension now; other domains when a real use needs them.

- **Depends on:** 141

- **Story:** As Dana, I want the compiler to know which keywords are core and which belong to the web extension, so that web concepts stay out of the core while every existing app keeps working.

- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**

  1. Given the compiler, When it resolves a file, Then keywords are partitioned into core and web (endpoint and its input, output, steps, respond with, the verbs, routes and status mapping), the web part loads deterministically when the file uses an endpoint, a verb or a route (implicit) or declares uses web (explicit), and the same input always loads the same set

  2. Given a file with no web construct, When a web keyword appears in a phrase template, Then it is an ordinary word as the grammar already says, and orders.phrase and every existing test, diagnostic and generated output stay byte-identical (the whole gate is green with no test edited except to add new ones)

  3. Given the later web cards (131, 133, 135 and the Tasks app), When they add GET, PUT, DELETE and route parameters, Then they extend the web part, not the core (a test lists the keywords of each part)



## Context



- No change to docs/GRAMMAR.md, docs/CHEATSHEET.md or tests/Phrase.Acceptance.Tests/Fixtures/orders.phrase (frozen, D72); the documentation split is card 143. The C# emitter (src/Phrase.Adapters.CSharp) stays unedited: the slice only partitions keywords in the compiler. The card must not delay cards 132 to 138: it changes where keywords are declared in the compiler, not what they do.
